title: Longest Valid Parentheses
statement: Given a string containing only the characters '(' and ')', return the length of the longest contiguous substring that is well-formed. A substring is well-formed when every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket after it and no closing bracket appears before its opener. The empty string is well-formed and has length 0.

examples.explanation: The longest well-formed substring is "()()", starting at index 1.

optimalComplexity: O(n) time, O(n) space — one pass with a stack of indices, seeded with -1 as the base for the first valid run.
rubric: Finds a linear solution rather than checking every substring.
Tracks indices, not just a counter — the length of a run is the distance between boundaries.
Handles a leading ')' and a trailing '(' without going negative or reporting a false match.
Returns 0 for the empty string and for input with no matched pair.
Can explain why the stack is seeded with a sentinel.
followUps: Can you do it in O(1) extra space? (two passes, left-to-right then right-to-left)
What if the string also contained square brackets that had to nest correctly?
How would you return the substring itself rather than its length?
